items.stem: A prompt returns a long paragraph, but the next system needs a JSON object with fixed keys. What is the most direct fix?

options.text: State the exact output format, including the required keys, in the prompt
options.rationale: Correct: specifying the output schema is the direct way to control answer shape.
Repeating an under-specified prompt tends to repeat the problem.

options.text: Make the prompt longer with more background
options.rationale: More background does not constrain the output shape.

options.text: Lower your expectations of the model
options.rationale: The fault is an unstated format requirement, not model capability.

items.explanation: Correct: specifying the output schema is the direct way to control answer shape.

items.stem: Which TWO choices make a prompt more repeatable across different inputs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Replacing the specific case with named input slots
options.rationale: Correct: parameterising inputs turns a one-off into a template.

options.text: Defining acceptance criteria for a correct answer
options.rationale: Correct: explicit criteria let you test the prompt on new inputs.

options.text: Relying on a single successful run as proof
options.rationale: One success does not establish reliability.

options.text: Removing all constraints so it is flexible
options.rationale: Removing constraints usually makes output less consistent.

items.explanation: Correct: parameterising inputs turns a one-off into a template.

items.stem: A single-shot prompt mislabels ambiguous support tickets. Adding what is most likely to help?

options.text: Two worked examples that cover the ambiguous cases
options.rationale: Correct: targeted examples steer the model on exactly the cases it gets wrong.
A vague exhortation gives the model no new signal.
Length does not address the labelling fault.
Removing structure would make the result harder to use, not more accurate.
